item.title: Warwick Will Aim High In Season 3!
item.description:
Warwick will aim high in Season 3!

Ahead of the largest student Mario Kart tournament in British History, I am sitting down with the teams fighting for the coveted title of the Best Mario Kart University. I had the pleasure of interviewing three competitors from Warwick to recap on how their debut season went, and to poke their heads about the upcoming competition.

I had the pleasure of speaking to Miku, a team captain from Warwick, alongside Jyrakeck and Sma, who both put in impressive performances last season.

I firstly asked the group about "how they found Season 2" and "if they did better than they thought they would", as pulling 5th in their first competitive outing was no easy feat. Jyrakeck mentioned that "5th was better than they thought they would have ever expected" and "they were very happy with the result" while Sma cited that "they felt like they outperformed their test matches prior to Season 2". The theme was an overall enjoyment!

A screenshot from the Birmingham VS Warwick match

When asked if there was a "particular performance from the team or individual that was inspired" Miku quickly jumped to mention their "impressive performance against Birmingham in Round 4", which many before the season might have seen as an upset. The consensus was common between the team that this was their magnum opus, while Jyrakeck also cited that "teammate 'v1p3r' was a turning point for the team" and "helped them consolidate their decision making and confidence". During the discussion it was plainly evident that the team had really bonded during the last twelve months.

A screenshot from the Warwick VS Keele match

Warwick suffered their only loss last season to eventual champions York. With this in mind, I asked the three if they "took anything away from the match" and if it "impacted their morale in any way". Sma said that the match was "a bit of a reality check" while Jyrakeck and Miku both ensured me that "it was important to have a competitive spirit, but you also have to remember to have fun". Expanding further on this point, Miku said that Warwick has "some of the most whimsy in how they play" and called back to when "they picked Baby Park in the first round of a match" and "swapped to Larry" because it was funny.

Speaking on behalf of everyone at UMKL, we love those small moments of students having fun together; it's one of the principles we were founded on!

In response to the previous comments I simply had to ask if they planned on going into Season 3 with that "a little bit of a laugh mentality" or if they were going to "put on a warface". This managed to get a split reaction from the team, with Sma mentioning that the very question was "in dispute right now". Jyrakeck followed this up by saying that a "balance needed to be struck" and "everyone has their own idea of having fun". This was proceeded by a very intriguing comment from the player, who was that he thought "some things needed to be retired" (referring to taking risks and their track selection process).

We could be seeing more calculated moves from Warwick this season...

It wouldn't be a proper interview about Season 3 if I didn't ask who they "wanted to avoid" and who they "wanted to face". Surprisingly, both Jyrakeck and Sma have their eyes set on the same target: Edinburgh. Jyrakeck mentioned "knowing people from Edinburgh" and "it would be a cool brag" while Sma said he wanted to play Edinburgh to "see how ridiculously good JoshAR is". Miku decided that Birmingham would be a good opponent in Season 3, to "see how far they had come" and cited the "local proximity" was a contributing factor. The consensus was to avoid "York" because of, and I quote, "PTSD". York have only lost one league match since the UMKL was established in 2024, to Staffs in the final match of Season 2.

I rounded out the interview by asking the three "where they were aiming for Season 3" and if they "had anything to say to the UMKL", and I got a clear consensus. Warwick want to push for Top Three this Season, with Miku saying they have "gotten a lot stronger" and "haven't lost any key players" and Sma saying "they have improved a lot over summer with their internal events". I was left with an intimidating quote from Jyrakeck at the end of the discussion, citing that the "Chips Will Fall As They May", and if their punching performance from last season was anything to go off I wouldn't write them off challenging for the whole thing.

Warwick have the energy and mindset to make a dent this season, and I for one can't help but get excited with them, and wish them the best of luck in the coming months. Season 3 will kick off in October 2026, stay tuned to witness the best British Student esports has to offer.

item.title: Website Redesign!
item.description:
The UMKL site has received a refresh, in-line with new brand guidelines, which will be published soon!

In preparation for Season 3, the UMKL website has been refreshed. Expect a more consistent brand style across all of the UMKL. Lots of news articles will be posted shortly, so be sure to check it out! Prepare to get excited as Season 3 is right around the corner!

Thanks to everyone who helped design and test the site! More content will be released soon.

The redesigned website has better support for higher resolution screens

Here is a full list of changes made to Cheep Cheep and the UMKL site below:

Cheep Cheep/Discord
- Fixed a bug that showed York as having 1 season win when they had 2
- Majorly refactored the bot's code base into cogs and folders for easier maintenance
- Added the ability for server members to /request-stream-key, /request-board-password and /request-media-password
- Added various admin commands
- Increased the team name length limit to 16 characters
- Added captchas that new members must complete before accessing all the channels in the server, sadly it's necessary as Discord can't make their own platform usable
- Added /export-my-data, which lets you download all the data UMKL holds on you
- Added automatic database backups
- Cheep Cheep now serves profile pictures and team emblems directly (used by the credits and teams pages)
- Added /change-team-name for admins
- Added Best Match Score leaderboards (season/lifetime, team/individual) to /leaderboards
- Team locations shown by Cheep Cheep now link to Google Maps
- Cheep Cheep now suggests using /disconnect when someone mentions disconnecting in a match chat
- Added fun dev commands
- Fixed various timezone and daylight saving time bugs affecting match and event times
- Fixed a bug where SP sometimes wasn't applied properly after a match ended
- Fixed a bug where SP history could be lost for some players
- Various performance improvements
- Fixed various bugs
- Fun fact Cheep Cheep runs on an AMD Ryzen 3 2200G with 16GB of RAM
- Another fun fact Cheep Cheep uses about 120MB of RAM
UMKL website
- Resigned entire website with a modern design
- Added a list of all teams underneath the current season's teams
- Added the ability to add a 'UMKL Matches' calendar to your calendar app
- Redesigned the live results page to work at any screen resolution, and with team parameters
- Made it obvious who the winner is on the teams page
- Rewrote all help/guide articles
- Added a downloadable assets pack containing team logos and emblems
- Added a search bar to the news page
- Revamped the tools page
- Various performance and page loading speed improvements across the site
- Added a disclaimer on the matches page for users viewing match times from outside the UK
- Fixed bugs and oversights

item.title: New app, Lakitu, now available on the UMKL Discord Server
item.description:
The UMKL development team has created a new app, Lakitu, for storing time trial records across all games in the Mario Kart series.

The Lakitu app has been in development for several months following a request from members of the UMKL board regarding the potential of bringing a time trial based competition to the UMKL. This app is a stepping stone towards that goal, with features for time trial competitions on the horizon.

The app, currently in an early-access state, is available on the UMKL Discord server. Users can register with the app, and submit their time trial records to it across every Mario Kart game. Users have the choice between submitting each of their lap times, or submitting the total time of the record to speed up the process. Users can also choose their character and vehicle combinations to provide more context for their record.

Lakitu allows users to set records across all popular categories in each game, such as shroomless or 200cc records. Users can view leaderboards for each category on each course, and can compare their times against all other submitted records for the chosen category. The app also integrates with the community made Mario Kart standards sheets, categorising records into tiers based on how close they are to the corresponding world record. As suitable standards sheets are not yet available for every category in every Mario Kart game, some standards were created by the development team to ensure every record can be categorised.Users can also use the app to track their total time across all courses in a given Mario Kart game. This requires the user to submit a record for every course.

The app has the ability to host time-limited competitions. These would involve a course being declared, on which users have a limited amount of time to set time trial records on. The user with the fastest time at the end of the competition will be declared the winner. The competitions have not been tested at scale yet as the feature is still in development. The first tests of this feature are likely to take place on the UMKL Discord server in the near future. This feature will not affect the normal operation of the UMKL, which will remain a team-based racing series when Season 3 begins later in the year.

The design of the app allows it to be added to any Discord server. However, this feature is restricted at the moment as the app is still in early access. Time trial records will be unique to each server that the app is added to, and server owners will be able to configure the various settings of the app to suit their needs.

The development of Lakitu is expected to continue alongside Cheep Cheep, the UMKL's master app that manages several aspects of the league. The UMKL development team asks users to report any issues they find with the app as this will allow bugs to be fixed before the app leaves its early access state.

Directions for joining the UMKL Discord server are available in the social links on the website.

item.title: Season 2 Round 1 Fixtures Revealed!
item.description:
The first round of Season 2 fixtures have been revealed, and we are kicking things off in style. In the coming weeks we will see 6 matches fought between 12 universities across the UK, and all of these will be live on the UMKL YouTube channel for you to enjoy!

Click here to see which matches will take place in round 1!

York VS Bristol

Our Season 1 title holders York are drawn against the oldest of newcomer teams Bristol. These teams last played a test match together in June, which fell in York's favour by a score of 516 - 468. Will York carry their momentum forward, or will Bristol upset the champions?

Staffs VS Glasgow

The runners up from Season 1 Staffs will be playing Glasgow in a chaotic first round tie. These teams have met once before, back in April with a victory in favour of Staffs. Can Glasgow bite back, or will Staffs continue their good run of form?

Edinburgh VS Brighton

The newest addition to the UMKL roster, Brighton, will face Season 1 veterans Edinburgh in their debut outing. With Edinburgh last playing back in February, Brighton could certainly test the waters and snatch a hard fought result. A fun watch is definitely in store with this fixture, but which team can take home the win?

Keele VS Sheffield

Uosheff might fancy their chances against Keele, who rounded off the table in their last outing. Keele last played a match in April, with a loss to their local rivals in Staffs, while Sheffield are yet to play a competitive fixture. Who will come out on top in this clash of underdogs?

Birmingham VS Liverpool

Our first clash of the newcomers sees Liverpool play Birmingham in a tantalising competitive debut. Birmingham have chalked up impressive results in test matches recently, against Warwick and Cambridge, but can Liverpool catch them by surprise in their first ever match?

Warwick VS Cambridge

A blockbuster tie sees Cambridge, with an upset win against York in their last match, against a red hot Warwick side in an action packed match, where the winner takes all. Which of these new teams will make their mark on an incredible first round in the new season?

Best of luck to all our teams, and may the best team win!

item.title: The Structure for Season 2
item.description:
The upcoming season of UMKL will be using a Swiss Style system to determine the winner, but what exactly is that?

A Swiss System Tournament, most commonly used in chess, draws opponents against each other based on their current standings and match records, resulting in closer matches and near accurate skill based matchmaking. This simply means that teams who win will play teams who win, and teams who lose will play teams who lose; there is no 'elimination' and everybody gets to keep on playing!

This system allows us to reduce the number of matchdays required for each team, which helps when most players are also full time students, and with the huge influx in teams this season it's just not feasible nor efficient to play almost 70 matches in the space of a few months.

With a Swiss System we reduce that number down to 24 matches, which will be closer fought and more entertaining for both players and the audience.

With Season 2 starting in October we hope that everyone enjoys the upcoming matches, and we look forward to seeing our teams back in action very soon!

This article is an explation of an announcement made on the UMKL Discord server, you can join the server here.

item.title: Join the UMKL Discord server!
item.description:
The UMKL Discord server is the heart of our operations and where our community lies.

From match organisation, to game results and general UMKL activity, the Discord server is the fastest way to keep up to date with the UMKL.

The server is also a thriving hub for all UMKL news, and is a great way to connect with other players and make friends across the UK.

With the Cheep Cheep app, users can fetch player and match data in the server.

Featured in our Discord server is our bespoke app - Cheep Cheep, ready to provide data about players in the UMKL, stats about teams. It can also manage a team's current roster before each match, and generate sleek custom images after every match, showing a team and player's score, along with the standings for a current season.
The Cheep Cheep app was developed by Adeola Adeniji, zy and Tushar Sundarka, please visit the credits for all UMKL credits.

It's also loaded with a bunch of tools helping board members manage matches and teams. This all ensures smooth running of the league.

The server is also the quickest way to contact the UMKL board, who are happy to answer any of your questions and queries. This is helpful for upcoming teams and universities who might be interested in taking part in future seasons.
Please visit the Joining Guide for more information on this topic.

Whether you're a player, a committee member or a fan, come join our Discord server and be a part of our lovely community!

You can join our Discord server here.

item.title: Welcome to the UMKL!
item.description:
Welcome to the UMKL!

If you've reached this page, you probably have an idea of what we do, but we'll explain more below!

We're an independent gaming league made up of university teams across the country, which compete in 6v6 Mario Kart 8 Deluxe matches.

This project started last year, where we had four university teams in play, but this has quickly expanded to universities across the country! Currently we're still growing, with 6v6 test matches and friendlies being played until our next season starts next academic year.

Season 2 is scheduled to start in October 2025.

We're one season down, with our reigning champions York topping the charts for Season 1.

Some team logos were incomplete during Season 1.

Currently, whilst we're working on our website and the next season's roster, we are currently having on-going test matches between our teams and practice rooms.

The UMKL Discord is growing daily, with more and more interest being shown in our matches and livestreams, as we carve out our own little niche in gaming culture.

We are run by students, for students, and remain dedicated to forging connections between universities. Our 6v6 comp format gives uni groups ample opportunity to communicate with each other, improve their Mario Kart 8 Deluxe skills, and grow as a team together.

With 12 players and 12 races per match, get ready to practice your green shell snipes, bomb throws, and to communicate effectively as a team to speed towards victory!

You can join our Discord server here.
Our YouTube channel, where we livestream matches, can be visited here.

Please visit the credits to see everyone who worked on the UMKL.
